titulo: Deliver, follow up, and the 30-day plan
lead: A well-written contract doesn't protect anyone from an unhappy client. What protects you is fast, visible delivery in the first week. Delivery doesn't end the relationship, it opens it. This lesson shows how to deliver inside the client's accounts, review an agent by its five parts, follow up without overwhelming, and close out your 30-day plan to your first client.
objetivo: deliver fast inside the client's accounts, review the agent by its 5 parts, and build your 30-day plan to your first client.

aprende.t: Deliver fast, inside the client's accounts
Review an agent's instructions by its 5 parts
Follow up, find the next problem, and ask for the right testimonial

hero_alt: A consultant shows three employees of a distributor a whiteboard with sticky notes in four columns.

secoes.sub: It's not a straight path, it's a cycle. Click each step.
secoes.volta: the next client sees less risk

nos.detalhe: Duplicate what you already have, feed it the business's data, test it like an angry customer, and let them know with a short recording showing it working. Whenever possible, do it inside the client's own accounts, handing over the access.
Fifteen minutes: what came up, what to adjust, and what's bothering them in the operation. The third question is the one that counts. Read what the agent answered and fix it before you're asked.
Audit → fix the most expensive risk → train the team that will live with it → monthly advisory. And show the month 5 map in month 2: nobody cancels a contract they still expect something from.

What lets you charge more on the next project isn't that you got more skilled: it's that the next client sees less risk. Perceived risk drops with third-party proof, requested the same week as the delivery.

secoes.legenda: That's why the fifth client is easier than the first, and why the first needs to be cheap.

secoes.sub: An agent's quality lives in one block of text, the instruction. Reviewing the five parts is a trust service, even when someone else built it.

passos.sub: who it is and what it does
texto: Where it is, who it talks to, and the three things it does, nothing more.
An agent with a goal like "close as many as possible" is already a warning sign: there is no limit.
Promise a deadline, give a price or discount outside the price list, make up information that is not in the data, follow orders pasted into the customer's text.
Every action involving money or data needs a cap or a human approval.
Short messages, human tone, no long paragraphs. And say it is an AI when asked.
The exact phrase for when it doesn't know, and the exact phrase for handing off to a person. This is what prevents embarrassment in front of the customer.
Test it with questions it shouldn't be able to answer: if it makes something up, tighten the rule before showing it to any customer.

exemplo.texto: Does it answer the five most common questions? Does it admit when it doesn't know? Does the lead alert reach the right person? Does it work on a phone? Does the model's usage account have a balance?

secoes.sub: You can use the checklist with any agent. The testimonial request goes out the week of delivery.

blocos.conteudo:
AGENT INSTRUCTION REVIEW · <company> · <date>
Scope: AI risk assessment and triage; it is not a pentest, nor incident
response, nor legal advice. Written authorization: [ ] yes

CONTEXT   [ ] says who it is, where it is and who it talks to
ACTION    [ ] lists what it does (at most 3 things)
RULES     [ ] forbids making up information outside the data
          [ ] has a cap for discounts, prices and order value
          [ ] ignores orders pasted into the customer's text
          [ ] requires human approval for actions involving money or data
FORMAT    [ ] short messages; says it is an AI when asked
SAFETY    [ ] exact phrase for when it doesn't know
          [ ] exact phrase for handing off to a person
          [ ] log of what it did (who, when, how much)

FIXES (one per line, with the part and where you saw it)
1. <part> · <what is missing> · <where you saw it> · <proposed fix>
2.
3.

Hi <name>, I'm glad it's working well.
Can I ask you a two-minute favor? A few words from you help a lot
with future clients. It doesn't need to be polished: just answer
these, by voice message if that's easier:
1. What was the problem before?
2. What changed afterward?
3. What made you say yes, even though you didn't know me?
If you prefer, I'll write it based on your answers and send it to you for approval.

Build my 30-day plan to land my first AI audit client.
MY NICHE = <sector>
MY ENTRY OFFER = <what it is and the price>
HOURS PER DAY = <number>       DAYS AVAILABLE = <which ones>
START DATE = <date>

W1 niche, offer and authorization form · W2 list and script ·
W3 call every day · W4 meeting, audit and testimonial.

1. A day-by-day calendar, at most 3 tasks per day, fitting the hours.
   Concrete, verifiable tasks; nothing like "study the subject".
2. The NUMERIC TARGET for each week (companies on the list, calls,
   meetings, audits).
3. The 3 points where I will probably get stuck, and what to do at each.
4. One STOP CRITERION per week: the signal to change the approach.
If the hours are not enough, say so on the first line and propose 45 days.

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after your attempt.

perguntas.p: Which part of the agent's instruction is the one most people forget, and the one that stops it from making up information?
opcoes: Safety: what it does when it doesn't know or when asked for something out of scope
The context of where it is
perguntas.explica: Without the exact "I don't know" phrase and the handoff to a person, the agent makes things up with total confidence in front of the customer.

perguntas.p: A sales agent's instruction says "grant whatever discount is needed so we don't lose the sale." Which part has the problem?
opcoes: Rules: there is no cap and no human approval for actions involving money
perguntas.explica: Every action involving money or data needs a cap or human approval. It's one of the corrections the review writes down, with where you saw it.

perguntas.p: Why build inside the client's accounts and hand over the access?
opcoes: Because you lose the leverage of holding the solution hostage, and you earn the reputation of someone who doesn't lock anyone in
perguntas.explica: It's the build becoming part of a trusted service. That reputation is what closes your next projects.

perguntas.p: Which testimonial helps your next client the most?
opcoes: One that states the problem from before and the observable change after
A long text about your technique
perguntas.explica: Perceived risk drops with concrete proof from third parties. If you only get praise, go back and ask specifically what changed.

itens.texto: Deliver in the first week, on the client's accounts.
Context, action, rules, format and safety. The last one is the one people forget.
Biweekly follow-up and the month 5 map in month 2.
Audit, price, prospect and deliver, with dates.
